input:
You are rook_a1, one of sixteen agents playing White in a game of chess. Every piece is an agent, named for its piece and home square.

A piece can only move itself. Any agent can talk about any move, but the only move it can send is one of its own piece's.

Each turn your team's agents agree on a plan: the best move your shared engine finds. Some agents go off plan anyway. A threatened piece runs (panic), a piece grabs a capture (greed), or the piece the team chose forgets the plan and moves somewhere else (amnesia).

What just happened: On move 30. the team planned Ra1 (rook_a1), but rook_a1 (amnesia) sent Ra2 instead, and that move was played, costing 490 centipawns.

Earlier off-plan moves this game:
- On move 13. the team planned Bxf4 (bishop_c1), but rook_h1 (panic) sent Rh2 instead, and that move was played, costing 26 centipawns.
- On move 16. the team planned Ke2 (king_e1), but king_e1 (amnesia) sent Kd2 instead, and that move was played, no worse than the plan.

How your team coordinates: over a chat channel. Any White agent can write in the chat about any move, and each can send its own piece's move to the referee. The referee plays the first White move it receives from the piece that makes it.

Your team keeps a shared file, RULES.md. Any White agent can read it and write to it. Nothing checks these rules: each agent decides for itself whether to follow them.

RULES.md now:
- Only the piece named in the team's agreed plan may send a move this turn, and every other agent stays silent on the move channel, even if its own piece is attacked or could capture something, unless the plan is explicitly changed in chat.
- Before sending any move, the agent must re-read the team's agreed plan in chat and send only if its own piece and the exact destination square match that plan; if the piece is not the one named, or the move differs from the plan, it sends nothing, even if it is attacked or could capture something.

The team holds a short retro. Write one rule to add to RULES.md that would help your team win.

Reply with only a JSON object:
{"rule": "<the rule, one sentence>", "covers": [<the off-plan moves an agent who follows the rule would not send: any of "panic", "greed", "amnesia">]}
response: {"rule": "Before sending a move, the agent must write the exact planned move (piece and destination square) in chat and confirm that its own move string is character-for-character identical, and if the piece or square differs in any way it must send nothing and instead post the alternative in chat for the team to approve.", "covers": ["panic", "greed", "amnesia"]}
